summary: Haruka Yanagisawa (1944–2015) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He held positions at Chiba University from approximately 1974 to 1994 and at the University of Tokyo from around 1994 to 2007.

Harumi Hirano Ziegler specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She studied at the University of California, Los Angeles, earning an MA by 1994 and a PhD by 2001 under doctoral supervisor Robert E. Buswell Jr.

Harunaga Isaacson is an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Groningen and Leiden under Hans T. Bakker and Tilmann Vetter. He held posts at Oxford, Hamburg, and the University of Pennsylvania, becoming professor at Hamburg in 2006.

Harushige Kōzu (1908–1973) was a linguist who studied under Naoshiro Tsuji at the University of Tokyo and at Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Tokyo from 1938 and became a professor and dean at Musashi University in 1968.

Harvey B. Aronson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies under Richard Hugh Robinson, was attested as a professor at the University of Virginia in 1988, and was co-director of the Dawn Mountain Center for Tibetan Buddhism in 2001.

Harvey Paul Alper (1945–1987) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Pennsylvania and served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at Southern Methodist University from 1974 to 1987.

Hasmukh Dhirajlal Sankalia (1908–1989) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied under Henry Heras and later with F. J. Richards at University College London, and served as a professor at Deccan College from 1945 to 1946.

Haya Akegarasu (1877–1954) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies figure who studied under Manshi Kiyozawa and at Otani University. He founded Seishinkai in 1901 and served as head of administration at Higashi Hongan-ji around 1951 to 1954.

Heather Stoddard specializes in Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at SOAS University of London between 1967 and 1970 under D. C. Lau, as well as under Nicole Vandier-Nicolas and Samten Gyaltsen Karmay.

Heeraman Tiwari is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He completed his D.Phil. at Oxford under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Richard Gombrich, joined Jawaharlal Nehru University around 2001, and held chair/fellowship posts at Heidelberg (2011–2012) and Hebrew University (2014–2015).
Hege Myrlund Larsen is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bergen under the supervision of Bruce Kapferer, attested in 2009.
Hegoda Khemananda is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1993, he was attested as Vice Principal at Vidyodaya Pirivena and Director at Dharma Paryeshanalaya.

Heidi Fjeld is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies. She earned her Doctor Rerum Politicarum under Signe Howell at the University of Oslo (2001–2006) and was a postdoctoral fellow there from around 2006 to 2010.
Heidi I. Koppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her MA at the University of Copenhagen under the supervision of Christian K. Wedemeyer, and also studied under Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi R. M. Pauwels is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She earned her PhD at the University of Washington under Alan Entwistle, lectured at SOAS (1994–1996), and became a professor at the University of Washington, where she was appointed in 1996.
Heidrun Brückner is an Indologist who studied under Wilhelm Rau. She held the Lehrstuhl für Indologie at the University of Würzburg from approximately 2001 to 2015.

Heike Oberlin is an Indologist who completed her PhD at Würzburg and her Habilitation at Tübingen. She held academic posts at Tübingen from 2005, serving as Associate Professor around 2011, and was a visiting professor at Sapienza in 2025.

Heimo Rau (1912–1993) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Vienna. He directed Goethe-Institut branches, taught at Freie Waldorfschule Uhlandshöhe, and was a PD at Heidelberg University from 1968 to 1982.

Hein Htet Kyaw is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, James Cook University, and Edinburgh Napier University. In 2024, he became Director of Australasia for Atheist Alliance International.

Heiner Eichner (1942–2024) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied under Karl Hoffmann at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg between roughly 1965 and 1974, and held a post at the University of Vienna from around 1989 to 2011.
